title: Per-layer scaling stabilizer and model-specific outlier policy for LLaMA / Mistral / Qwen quant pipelines
creator: Asha Nair
description: Goal: reduce regressive accuracy spikes introduced by per-layer quant scaling for LLaMA, Mistral, and Qwen model families while preserving the unit-cost benefits of FP8 and INT8 profiles. Scope covers: (1) a hardened per-layer scaling "stabilizer" that applies conservative damping to scale updates when calibration histograms contain heavy-tailed activations, (2) a model-specific outlier handling policy that chooses between clipping, stochastic rounding, or per-channel re-scaling, and (3) an automated calibration annealing schedule used in CI to avoid overfitting to a small calibration corpus. We will produce updated quant profiles and calibration artifacts and validate with the canonical Redwood suite (generation LM evals, embedding MSE, and downstream retrieval QA checks). This ticket replaces ad-hoc per-layer fixes with a reproducible pipeline, telemetry hooks for layer-level failure modes, and rollout gating in the console.
requirements: Implement per-layer scaler with configurable damping coefficient and 'holdout' threshold
Expose model-specific policy switch (clip|stochastic_round|per_channel_rescale) in calibration config
Add CI job that runs hybrid FP8/INT8 calibration with annealing (multi-seed) and stores per-layer histograms to GCS
Integrate layer-level regression alerts into Console (notify on >0.5% BLEU/ROUGE/EM degradation over baseline)
Provide migration plan for existing runtime profiles (safe fallback to previous profile on SLO/accuracy regression)
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline produces deterministic profile artifacts reproducible across 3 seeds
No production model experiences >1% top-line generation-quality regression vs current baseline after rollout in canary (2000 prompts)
Per-layer telemetry shows <0.1% of layers under 'unstable' classification across the canary set
Console rollout gating blocks profile promotion on accuracy regression and triggers automatic fallback to prior profile
Documentation and runbook published for calibrators and SREs
implementation_notes: Use per-layer L2 / MAD statistics instead of only max-activation to reduce sensitivity to single-shot spikes
Damping: if layer histogram kurtosis > K_threshold, multiply proposed scale update by 0.3 and increase clipping aggressiveness
Annealing schedule: start with conservative clipping for first 2k samples then relax over additional 8k samples; average scales across windows

Model-specific heuristics: LLaMA defaults to per_channel_rescale + mild clipping, Mistral prefers stochastic_round for FFN layers, Qwen uses hybrid FP8 for attention and INT8 for FFN with per-layer guard
Record KV-cache precision mismatch checks — mismatched precision between generation warmup and steady-state can surface false outliers
validation_plan: Run full CI calibration on representative shards for each model family (LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen) with 5 random seeds
Evaluate on Redwood eval set: perplexity/regression on prompt completions, embedding cosine similarity, and downstream RAG QA metrics
Noise-injection test: add synthetic outlier spikes to 1% of calibration samples to verify damping prevents scale collapse
A/B canary: route 5% traffic of non-enterprise customers to profile candidate for 72 hours, collect token-level latency and accuracy deltas
Post-rollout verification: automated job comparing production logs to baseline for 7 days; auto-rollback if regressions persist
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-conservative damping reduces effective dynamic range and increases token generation errors — Mitigation: tune damping coefficient per model family and add per-layer exception list
Risk: Calibration corpus bias causing profile mismatch — Mitigation: increase corpus diversity and use annealed averaging across windows
Risk: Increased calibration CI time — Mitigation: sample-based validation and early-exit when candidate is within acceptance bounds
Risk: Telemetry volume — Mitigation: aggregate histograms client-side and push sampled summaries
